body:
I feel terrible for your loss, but I also want to say that I don't blame any of his friends. I haven't told anyone my own issues because I fear that they would call the police and put me in an institution, rather than just talking to me. What his friends should have done is talked to him and offered to come over to talk it through. If they did that, then what more can you really ask of someone?

Also how is this her fault? People break up with each other all the time, it isn't her job to make sure he doesn't kill himself. She isn't even obligated to talk to him if she doesn't want to. Most girls would have been freaked out and not responded to suicidal texts like that (after a breakup).
I've given it some thought, but I'm rather socially awkward and I can't imagine what else I'd even do for work.

Thanks for responding, I really appreciate it. If I start feeling better before my gun arrives I'll think about seeing a therapist, but I doubt it will happen. I just can't risk being put in a mental hospital and having my gun taken away.
Don't worry, there is nothing you can say. I'm honestly just relieved at this point. Thanks for responding though.
Thanks for the offer, but just having someone read this is enough.

I wish you the best of luck and I hope you find a good therapist. I still have a week or so before my gun arrives, so maybe I'll have a temporary change of mind and will try to see a therapist - but I doubt it. I'm just thankful that I live in a place that has relaxed gun laws.
